design: The benchmark paragraph, one sentence per row, composed by trailmend.eval.benchmark from the evidence files named in each row's sources and from nothing else. A sentence is only written in its strong form when the numbers support it; otherwise it states what was measured. `facts` holds every number a sentence uses.

rows.text: I tested TrailMend on 3 generated company graphs (1,165 nodes, 124 to 126 planted faults each) and on MetaQA, a public movie knowledge graph (134,741 triples, 360 held-out questions per seed, 3 seeds, half the triples withheld).

Run 2's shared graph carried stray edges from earlier runs, so it was replicated on an emptied HydraDB (run 3dbcdf3-580ae8dc): the full loop went from 77.0% to 84.6% against 77.0% for the frozen graph, which reproduced the gain; run 2's own numbers below stay as recorded.

After 5 rounds of learning from its own answers, held-out accuracy on the company graphs rose from 77.9% to 85.7% (p < 0.001 on a paired test, every seed), and held-out Hits@1 on MetaQA rose from 55.3% to 71.5% (p < 0.001 on a paired test, every seed).
It captured 69% of the gain that perfect repairs would give on the company graphs and 38% on MetaQA.

Random reweighting, matched to its own targeted plan's number and size of cost changes each round, ends at 76.6% on the company graphs against 77.9% for the untouched graph, and at 55.6% on MetaQA against 55.3% for the untouched graph, and random reweighting did not significantly beat the untouched graph on any seed. The random arm reads no new documents; gap-fill alone, with no reweighting, reaches 82.9% on the company graphs.

A plain document store over the same corpus stays flat at 28.3% (15.5% on MetaQA) because it has no links for the loop to repair, and on the clean replication, the same loop with unweighted search goes from 83.3% to 89.9%, 5.3 points above the loop that searches on cost on the same graph (significantly higher on 3 of 3 seeds, significantly lower on 0).

Wrong answers fell 30% on the company graphs and fell 9% on MetaQA, and 1,386 of 1,393 held-out questions that were right at the start were still right at the end, with every break along the way traced to a receipt.

The graph did get bigger, but only by reading: the company graphs gained 158 links (3.2%), each from a withheld document and each under a receipt, and MetaQA read back 5,684 withheld triples. Reweighting and quarantine also change the graph; these results do not isolate their gain from gap-fill.
